title: Unveiling the biological effects of radio-frequency and extremely-low frequency electromagnetic fields on the central ne

predicted_errors.error_location: Opening numbered section 1 (sentences about IoT/GPS, medical imaging, scientific progress)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites refs 1-3 for claims about IoT/GPS/media, medical X-rays/radiation therapy, and progress of sciences, but the visible reference list identifies ref 1 as Takebayashi et al. (brain tumour case-control), ref 2 as Jimenez et al. (cancer treatment), and ref 3 as Pall et al. (neuropsychiatric effects). These references do not support the claims, indicating misattributed or misnumbered citations.

Ezz et al. is cited as ref 468, Maaroufi et al. as ref 469, Kim et al. as ref 470, etc. The reference numbering elsewhere in the article runs only up to about 158; these out-of-range citations are inconsistent with the paper's bibliography and appear to be imported from another manuscript.

The text states that dopamine 'is also secreted from the pituitary gland'. Dopamine is produced/released by hypothalamic neurons and acts on the anterior pituitary, but it is not a pituitary secretion.
The text refers to 'inhibitory neurotransmitters such as Acetylcholine'. Acetylcholine is predominantly excitatory or modulatory, not a canonical inhibitory neurotransmitter like GABA or glycine.

predicted_errors.error_location: Brain tumor / ELF-EMF section, Ahlbom et al. pooled analysis paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states '99.2% of children residing in households with exposure levels below 0.4 μT exhibited a lower risk... 0.8% of children exposed to 0.4 μT or higher displayed relatively elevated risk estimates.' These percentages describe the exposure distribution in the pooled study, not the proportion of children exhibiting lower/elevated risk; this misrepresents the statistical result.

The text states 'The association between ELF-EMF exposure and cancer was first articulated in 1979...' then states 'In 1976, Wertheimer and Leeper put forth a hypothesis...' These claims are chronologically inconsistent; if the association was first articulated in 1979, a 1976 Wertheimer and Leeper hypothesis cannot precede it.

predicted_errors.error_location: Burman et al. description in the ELF-EMF animal-studies paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text describes 'a power of 8.56 V/m r.m.s (on-state) and 4.99 V/m r.m.s (off-state)'. The unit V/m is an electric field strength, not a power, so the description is physically inconsistent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Takebayashi et al. sentence in RF-EMR/cancer introductory discussion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says '322 individuals with tumors exposed to RF-EMR with SAR values below 0.1 W/kg were examined', but Takebayashi et al. is a case-control study that enrolled brain tumour cases and controls and estimated/assigned SAR; it did not simply examine 322 tumour patients exposed below 0.1 W/kg.

predicted_errors.error_location: Brain development / prenatal exposure paragraph (Bas et al.)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'During the prenatal period, Bas et al exposed juvenile rats to RF-EMR...' Prenatal period and juvenile rats are inconsistent developmental stages; exposure would have been during gestation with postnatal/juvenile assessment, not exposure of juvenile rats prenatally.
